newsitem.title: CANADA: Monsanto Canada recalls transgenic canola.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto Canada recalls transgenic canola.

text.p: Monsanto Canada recalled two herbicide-resistant, genetically altered canola seed varieties, Monsanto Canada vice-president Ray Mowling told Reuters.
"There's been a recall of two varieties of seed. Limagrain is actually the seed company and our seed partner on this and they are two Round-Up Ready canola varieties," Mowling said.
Canadian oilseed traders and brokers cited rumours of a Monsanto seed recall removing up to 10 percent of available canola seed ahead of spring planting.
"The impact overall to total canola planting should be nil because the majority of the seed has not been planted," he said.
Ten Alberta farmers planted the two recalled varieties, he added.
"In terms of total, overall canola planting this is a very, very minor issue," Mowling said.
"What the grower will not be able to have, or at least some, is access to Round-Up Ready canola seed," he said.
United Grain Growers Ltd on April 2 forecast western Canadian canola seeded acreage at 12.17 million acres this spring compared to 8.8 million last spring.
Canola oil has the lowest saturated fat level of any cooking oil at 7.0 percent and the seeds are a major export to Japan.
